newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Aluminium Bahrain in $23.6 mln shipping terminal.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium Bahrain in $23.6 mln shipping terminal.

text.p: Aluminium Bahrain BSC (Alba) said work had started on an 8.9 million dinar ($23.6 million) project to build a shipping terminal to handle liquid pitch.
An Alba newsletter said the project was in line with the company's plan to switch to the more environmentally-friendly liquid form of the raw material.
Alba, the biggest aluminium producer in the Middle East, has invested $250 million in advanced fume treatment systems to minimise the environmental impact of its operations.
The terminal is being built alongside existing facilities handling alumina and petroleum coke. Solid pitch is mixed with petroleum coke to make the anodes used in the production of aluminium.
Alba, which currently consumes 45,000 tonnes of pitch a year, said the terminal was due to be completed in May 1998.

With production capacity of more than 460,000 tonnes a year, the smelter is 77 percent owned by the Bahraini government and 20 percent by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. German group Breton Investments holds the rest.
